item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports improving negative selection and loss calibration before changing the BERT4Rec backbone. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) identifies a sampled-softmax bias: the positive is always included, whereas negatives are sampled. Its refined correction treats these contributions separately and introduces an uncertainty-dependent weight. This addresses sampling bias, not false-negative labels. [Improved Estimation of Ranks (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06371) corrects sampled rank estimates, enabling efficient WARP/LambdaRank optimization; relevant when considering ranking losses instead of softmax. Neither establishes gains on the four target Amazon categories.\n\nHardest-only mining risks emphasizing unobserved positives. [EMM (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0893608026004090) reports a controlled hard–random mixture with ID exclusion and similarity-window filtering for contrastive recommendation. Its safeguards are transferable hypotheses, rather than validated BERT4Rec improvements. A practical experiment would retain masked-target training and appended-mask inference, compare uniform sampled softmax against a gradually introduced moderate-hard/random mixture, exclude known training positives and duplicate candidates, and cap or downweight extreme-hard negatives. If approximating full softmax, correction must match the actual proposal distribution; deterministic top-k mining cannot simply inherit uniform-sampling correction. Train these objectives within one BERT4Rec per category, with no inference fusion. Select using fixed macro validation HR@10 across all four categories; inspect Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics separately, but do not infer improvement from larger training margins."}
